Now I have everything needed.

## Top 5 ready tasks

1. **`bp-login-ux-w2-live-e2e`** — *Device-login loop witnessed live: real TTY + real browser on barkpark.cloud, evidence stamped.* Run the real `bp login` device-code flow against the live control plane (real terminal + real browser, isolated scratch config) and durably capture evidence for every stage of the flow; 7 of 8 acceptance criteria are already proven, with only a human-gated paid-fleet step outstanding.

2. **`task-96a908af98698118`** — *Felix pristine initiative — Phoenix mastery audit of api/.* A large audit epic (101 children) that compares Barkpark's Elixir/Phoenix code against the "Phoenix Mastery Corpus," accepting a fix only if it prevents a named failure mode, removes measured cost, closes a real risk class, or provably cheapens a future change — explicitly rejecting pure tidiness/idiom churn.

3. **`gh-1`** — *GitHub App registration + credential wiring.* A human-only gate task: register Barkpark Cloud's GitHub App (Contents/Administration/Webhooks permissions) and wire its four credentials into `cloud/docker-compose.yml` so the live "Connect GitHub" repo-provisioning feature can go live instead of staying fail-closed.

4. **`bp-cloud-build-epic`** — *Perfect Plan BUILD — ship the readiness-ledger sequence into Barkpark Cloud.* The execution epic (41 children) turning the ratified "readiness ledger" plan into shipped tenancy primitives — complete per-workspace export/import, a unified content+media quota/telemetry gate, an audited workspace-delete HTTP route, and doc corrections.

5. **`task-e640bb01fca6ea38`** — *Barkpark Connectors — integrate agents with external services (epic).* A large epic (141 children) to make connecting a Barkpark agent to external services (chat channels like Slack/Discord/Telegram, and MCP tool connectors like GitHub/Linear) a first-class, two-minute, multi-tenant product action.

## Two manifest facts

- **(a) Ready task volume:** `bp task ready` returned a page capped at the server's default limit of 50, with the tool itself warning "more may be available — re-run with `--all`" — so there are at least 50 ready tasks in the queue, possibly more.
- **(b) Busiest noun:** `doc` carries the most commands in the manifest — 17 (`get`, `ls`, `backlinks`, `related`, `history`, `revision`, `restore-revision`, `query`, `mutate`, `publish`, `unpublish`, `discard-draft`, `delete`, `create`, `create-or-replace`, `create-if-not-exists`, `patch`), edging out `media` at 16 and `task` at 13.

No writes, claims, or file modifications were performed — everything above came from read-only `bp capabilities`, `bp task ready`, and `bp task get` calls.
